general: Screening for, and treatment of, aetiologies, and CV and non-CV comorbidities is recommended in patients with HFpEF.
Diuretics are recommended in congested patients with HFrEF to alleviate symptoms and signs.
recommendations_prevention_of_chronic_HF: Treatment of hypertension is recommended to prevent or delay onset of HF and to prevent HF hospitalizations.
Treatment with statins is recommended in patients at high risk of CV disease or with CV disease to prevent or delay onset of HF and to prevent HF hospitalizations.

SGLT2 inhibitors (canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, ertugliflozin, sotagliflozin) are recommended in patients with diabetes at high risk of CV disease or with CV disease to prevent HF hospitalizations.
Counselling against sedentary behaviour, obesity, cigarette smoking, and alcohol abuse is recommended to prevent or delay onset of HF.
other_recommendations_management_chronic: Enroll HF patients in a multidisciplinary HF management programme to reduce risk of HF hospitalization and mortality.
Self-management strategies are recommended to reduce the risk of HF hospitalization and mortality.
Home-based and/or clinic-based programmes improve outcomes and are recommended to reduce the risk of HF hospitalization and mortality.
Exercise is recommended for all patients who are able in order to improve exercise capacity and quality of life and reduce HF hospitalization.
recommendations_treatment_advanced_HF: Patients being considered for long-term mechanical circulatory support (MCS) must have good compliance, appropriate capacity for device handling and psychosocial support.
Heart transplantation is recommended for patients with advanced HF refractory to medical/device therapy who do not have absolute contraindications.
recommendations_treatment_acute_HF: Oxygen is recommended in patients with SpO2 <90% or PaO2 <60 mmHg to correct hypoxaemia.
Intubation is recommended for progressive respiratory failure persisting despite oxygen administration or non-invasive ventilation.
Intravenous loop diuretics are recommended for all patients with acute HF admitted with signs/symptoms of fluid overload to improve symptoms.
Thromboprophylaxis (e.g., with LMWH) is recommended in patients not already anticoagulated and with no contraindication to anticoagulation to reduce risk of venous thrombosis and pulmonary embolism.
Inotropic agents are not recommended routinely; use only for patients with symptomatic hypotension and evidence of hypoperfusion.
Routine use of opiates is not recommended, unless in selected patients with severe/intractable pain or anxiety.
Intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) is not routinely recommended post-MI cardiogenic shock.
post_discharge_management_after_HF_hospi: Patients hospitalized for HF should be carefully evaluated to exclude persistent signs of congestion before discharge and to optimize oral treatment.
Where possible, evidence-based oral medical treatment should be administered before discharge.
An early follow-up visit (1–2 weeks after discharge) is recommended to assess signs of congestion, drug tolerance, and to start/continue uptitration of evidence-based therapy.
recommendations_HF_with_AF: Long-term treatment with an oral anticoagulant is recommended in all patients with AF, HF, and CHA2DS2-VASc score ≥2 in men or ≥3 in women.
Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are recommended in preference to VKAs in patients with HF, except in those with moderate or severe mitral stenosis or mechanical prosthetic heart valves.
Urgent electrical cardioversion (ECV) is recommended in the setting of acute worsening of HF in patients presenting with rapid ventricular rates and haemodynamic instability.
Treatment with certain antiarrhythmic agents (flecainide, encainide, disopyramide, dronedarone, and D-sotalol) is not recommended due to safety concerns.
